All variables (e.g., `_gitauthor`, `pkgname`, `source`, `sha256sums`) are defined with straightforward string or array expressions that do not involve command substitution, external downloads, or execution of external code. The source URLs point to the declared GitHub repository and are constructed predictably from version and architecture variables. There are no calls to `curl`, `wget`, `eval`, or other potentially dangerous commands at the global scope.

While the checksums for sources are provided and valid (none are set to 'SKIP'), even if they were missing or skipped, that would not affect the safety of running `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, as no sources are downloaded or verified during this step. Therefore, sourcing this PKGBUILD for metadata extraction poses no risk of remote code execution or data exfiltration.
</details>
